facts.text: The IMF raised South Korea's 2026 growth forecast to 3.3 percent (3.3%), up 0.7 percentage points (0.7 points) from its July projection.
Strong semiconductor exports, driven by AI infrastructure demand, more than offset the fallout from the Middle East war.
Choi Ji-young, executive director of the IMF Asia and Pacific Constituency Office: "Building AI data centers takes a long time, potentially around 10 years."
Choi: Korea could face a stock market correction, an adjustment in its current account and adverse effects on businesses should the AI boom falter.
The government plans to launch a Future Fund next year, funded by windfall revenue from the chip supercycle.

sources.title: AI boom to sustain Korea amid global headwinds for years, says senior IMF official

caption:
AI chips just moved a whole country's forecast.

The IMF raised South Korea's 2026 growth outlook to 3.3%, up 0.7 points since July. The driver: semiconductor exports riding AI infrastructure demand.

→ “Building AI data centers takes a long time, potentially around 10 years.” (IMF's Choi Ji-young)
→ The risk: a stock market correction if the AI boom falters
→ Next: a “Future Fund” paid for by chip windfall revenue

Source: Korea JoongAng Daily / Yonhap, Oct 18, 2026.
